best_for: Windows desktop tinkerers who want live meters for CPU, memory, music or weather on the desktop, and who enjoy picking skins made by other people.

points.title: An engine for skins
points.text: Rainmeter shows small widgets, called skins, on your desktop, from hardware meters to audio visualizers. It comes with a few starter skins; most of the good ones are made by the community and installed separately.

points.title: Light on your PC
points.text: The project says it uses very little of your hardware, so meters can stay on screen all day without slowing games or work.

points.title: Free and open since 2001
points.text: It costs nothing and has been open source under GPL v2 since 2001, with the code on GitHub.

points.title: Windows only, back to Windows 7
points.text: It runs on Windows 7 with Service Pack 1 and the Platform Update, up to Windows 11. There is no Mac or Linux version.

points.title: Portable if you want it
points.text: The standard install goes to Program Files and can start with Windows. A portable install runs from one folder, such as a USB stick, and leaves the registry and Start menu alone. New installs use the 64-bit build on 64-bit Windows.

points.title: Admin prompt on install
points.text: The installer listed here installs for all users, so it asks for administrator approval unless you run it from an admin prompt. The Windows listing keeps 9 versions.
